clue.text: His eccentric way to convey birthday wishes?

parts.note: read as the plural of the greeting 'hi', so several hellos or salutations
a card is an odd or comical person, an eccentric

explanation.surface: A quirky man has his own odd way of sending birthday wishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His' looks like a possessive, but it is read as the plural of 'Hi!': a set of salutations.
explanation.definitionFit: A printed card sent with good wishes is the usual way to mark someone's birthday.

clue.text: He trained with a protege — with one expected to bring glory to team

definitions.text: one expected to bring glory to team

indicators.note: trained suggests being drilled into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A coach worked with a young protege who is tipped to win honours for the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' sits between the fodder words: the letters of HE and WITH A PROTEGE are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a person on whom high hopes of success rest, originally a boxing challenger.

clue.text: Encourage, say, half-hearted fool

parts.note: eg, for example, is signalled by say

indicators.note: the heart of the word for fool is its double O; half of that is removed

parts.note: a goon is a fool or idiot

explanation.surface: Someone urges on a fool who is only half committed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' removes one of the two middle Os of GOON, leaving GON.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge someone on or spur them to act is to encourage them.

clue.text: Mean business, so come straight here —- how apt

definitions.text: Mean business, so come straight here
definitions.meaning: someone who means business comes straight to the crux of the matter

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition plays on the phrase 'come straight to the ...', where the answer fills the gap that 'here' marks.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means relevant and concise, and it is also where a direct speaker comes straight to.

clue.text: Tip off writer going to beat club

parts.note: a nib is the writing tip of a pen, the writer
to lick is to beat or thrash

explanation.surface: Someone warns an author before attacking him with a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip off' looks like a warning, but it is the nib, the tip of a pen (the writer). A NIBLICK is an old name for a golf club like a nine iron.
explanation.definitionFit: A niblick is an old-fashioned golf club with a steeply angled face.

clue.text: Work out what prince royal might do

definitions.meaning: to work out is to turn out well, to be a success
a royal prince may follow his parent on the throne

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to turn out well and to take over a title or throne from a predecessor.

clue.text: Angers clergyman, perhaps, with extract from Jabberwocky

indicators.note: an extract is a short piece taken from within, so the letters lie inside the word

explanation.surface: A churchman gets angry when quoted a passage from Lewis Carroll's nonsense poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angers' looks like a verb but is the French city of Angers, so the clergyman is a French one.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbe is a French cleric, the kind of clergyman found in a French city such as Angers.

clue.text: Re-united clan held a disco here once?

indicators.note: reunited suggests the members coming back together in a new grouping, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clan gathered again and threw a disco at the venue.
explanation.definitionFit: A dance hall was a public venue for dancing, where discos might be held in years past.

clue.text: Rough tyke's blue joke finally ending weakly

parts.note: shaggy means rough or unkempt
a tyke is a dog, so tyke's is dog's
blue is the colour of the UK Conservatives, so a blue is a Tory

explanation.surface: A rough dog tells a crude joke that peters out at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' seems to mean rude, but it stands for TORY, a member of Britain's Conservative Party, whose colour is blue.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of tale is a long rambling joke with a deliberately feeble punchline.

clue.text: Chaps having row put away after hearing

indicators.note: the word for put away is heard spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: to put away food is to eat it, so put away gives ate

explanation.surface: Some men who had an argument cleared off once their case was heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel, but it means rowing: a rowing crew of this size.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing crew of that many oarsmen is called by the number, so it is men who row.

clue.text: Like MP, but not minister, with second seat

parts.note: to second someone is to back or support them
a bench is a seat

explanation.surface: An MP without office gets a seat once his motion is seconded.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK Parliament, MPs who are not ministers sit on the rear benches.
explanation.definitionFit: Backbench describes an ordinary member of parliament who holds no government post.

clue.text: Bananas ain't greens, they're fruit

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone insists bananas are not greens but fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like part of the fruit picture, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangerines are small citrus fruits, like mandarins.

clue.text: In short, it's the main danger

definitions.text: In short, it's the main danger

parts.words: In short, it's the main danger
parts.note: the main is the sea, and the hazard it holds is a floating mass of ice, here named in shortened form

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a short form of the name for a floating ice mass, a danger to shipping at sea.

clue.text: Deed Moslem converts regarded as interfering

indicators.note: converts means changes into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A deed by a Muslim convert is seen as interference.
explanation.definitionFit: Meddlesome describes someone who pokes into other people's affairs, a synonym of interfering.

clue.text: This man pretended to protect source of lethally poisonous drug

parts.note: this man is he

indicators.note: protecting is surrounding, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: mock as an adjective means sham or pretended

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A man feigned protecting the source of a deadly poison.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemlock is a poisonous plant, and the drug made from it killed Socrates.

clue.text: Person driving car without current tax?

indicators.note: without is used in the old sense of outside, so the car goes around the rest

parts.note: a motor is a car
I is the physics symbol for electric current
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: Someone is caught driving a car with no up-to-date road tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but is the old sense 'outside', so the car surrounds the current and the tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A motivator is someone who drives others on, a person who supplies drive.

clue.text: Journal with extremely explicit entry about food?

indicators.note: the letters are entered into the journal, placed inside it

parts.note: a diary is a journal

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A diary contains a very frank entry on eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Dietary is an adjective meaning concerning diet, so it is about food.

clue.text: Huge bird taking a short cut

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
taken as written

indicators.note: short means cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a nick is a small cut

explanation.surface: A huge bird takes a shortcut.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanic means of gigantic size, from the Titans of Greek myth.

clue.text: Voucher for buying drink mainly, not for red wine

indicators.note: mainly means most of it, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a chit is a note or voucher, used for buying drinks on account
anti means against, not for

explanation.surface: A voucher meant mostly for drink is not valid for red wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from Tuscany.

clue.text: Heathen spurned in one old opera

indicators.note: to spurn is to reject, so the word in is thrown out

parts.note: an infidel is an unbeliever, a heathen
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A pagan is rejected in an old opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word, but it is the piece 'spurned' removes from INFIDEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidelio is Beethoven's only opera.

clue.text: Lose fish dropped in well

indicators.note: the fish is dropped inside the other word

parts.note: fit means well or healthy
an orfe is a freshwater fish, the ide

explanation.surface: Someone loses a fish down a well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' looks like a water well, but it means healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: To forfeit something is to lose it as a penalty.

clue.text: Sailor's raised in coastal town

definitions.meaning: in nautical usage the past tense of heave, to raise or haul, takes this old form
a seaside town in Sussex, next to Brighton

explanation.walkthrough: HOVE is a seaside town in East Sussex, England, beside Brighton.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the sailors' past tense of heave, and also a Sussex seaside town.

clue.text: Passion rife in play with moving scenes

indicators.note: in play suggests the letters being toyed with, so they are rearranged
moving means shifting about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Passion is everywhere in a play with emotional scenes.
explanation.walkthrough: Two anagrams: 'in play' turns RIFE into FIER, and 'moving' turns SCENES into CENESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Fierceness is intensity of feeling, a fit synonym for passion.

clue.text: Old craft capsizing more than usually

parts.note: ex means former or old

indicators.note: capsizing in a down clue turns the word upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: art is craft or skill

explanation.surface: An old boat overturns in unusual conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like a boat, but it means skill: ART, which 'capsizing' turns to TRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra as an adverb means especially or more than usually, as in extra careful.

clue.text: Empty rooms

definitions.meaning: a tyre or battery with nothing left in it is described this way
a set of rooms forming a home on one floor

explanation.definitionFit: The word means deflated or drained, and also an apartment, a set of rooms.

clue.text: Peevishness shown by girl after losing head

parts.note: Petula is a girl's name, as in the singer Petula Clark

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: once can mean after, as in once he left

explanation.surface: A girl shows bad temper after being beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' looks like a placing word, but it is the conjunction sense, as in 'once you arrive'; 'losing head' drops its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Petulance is childish sulky bad temper, which is peevishness.

clue.text: Cap or old hat will go with suit

parts.note: something old hat is out of fashion, so out
to do is to suit or serve, as in that will do

explanation.surface: A cap or an outmoded hat will match a suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cap' looks like headwear in the picture of hats, but it means to top or surpass.
explanation.definitionFit: To cap someone's achievement is to better or surpass it.

clue.text: Spending one's way out of a depression?

definitions.text: Spending one's way out of a depression?

parts.words: Spending one's way out of a depression?
parts.note: sounds like an economic recovery plan, but describes a gloomy person going shopping to cheer up

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a jocular name for shopping to lift one's mood, beating low spirits by spending.
